newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank raises merger benefit target.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank raises merger benefit target.

text.p: NationsBank Corp investor relations executive Susan Carr said in a telephone conference with reporters that the company is raising its 1999 target for merger beneflts from its acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares to $600 million from $515 million.
Carr said the new projection is based on an estimated increase in the 17 percent range for both revenue enhancements and expense savings. Carr spoke from the bank's headquarters in Charlotte, N.C.
The old figure of $515 million consisted of about $335 million in expense savings and $180 million in revenue enhancement.
Carr said the merger benefit figure remains $265 million for this year and she said NationsBank is "very comfortable" with a merger benefit target of $460 million for 1998.
NationsBank acquired St. Louis-based Boatmen's on January 7, 1997.
Carr said merger integration "continues on track and even ahead of schedule a little bit."
Carr said employees now have a "market-based focus" after concentrating on the transition and integration.
"Momentum has picked up as we move into the second half," she said. "We feel like the second half is starting out strongly."

She said the charge-off rate in the managed credit card portfolio was 6.23 percent in the second quarter of 1997 versus 6.09 percent in the first quarter. She said it was the smallest increase in several quarters.
